content.thinking: archiveMember appears to set a suspended status.

archiveMember incorrectly sets member status to "suspended", conflating removal with suspension.

The user clarified that removal is unchanged and a removed member is not suspended. I need to decide whether to preserve the current archiveMember behavior or fix it.

findMemberById does not filter archived members, so removed members still carry a "suspended" status. The task requires that archived members throw NotFoundError on lookup.

I am weighing whether to stop setting status to "suspended" on archive. If I leave the current behavior, suspended live members and removed members are still distinguishable by archivedAt.
Reviewing the usage repository seat count query and digest service recipient selection.

I need to understand how activity records relate to members.

I need to add member.suspended and member.reinstated audit actions to ActivityAction, the Zod schema, activity listeners, and labels. Tests for member services, permissions, seat counts, and digest emails must be updated to exclude suspended owners.

Notifications must skip suspended members. Mention resolution should filter out suspended users, but the member list itself should still include them. Before inserting or assigning an assignee, I need to look up the member by userId and throw a MemberSuspendedError if they are suspended.

I should only throw a MemberSuspendedError when the member is actually suspended; if the member is missing, the existing path continues. I also need to check the updateIssue schema for assigneeId handling.

For suspension rules: self-suspension is forbidden. An admin cannot suspend an owner because owners outrank admins. Owners may suspend other owners at the same rank.

The last-owner check must exclude suspended owners from the remaining owner count. The current assertion counts all owners in the list, but it should only count non-suspended ones.

Demoting or removing an owner should exclude suspended members from the remaining owner count. If the only other owner is suspended, the workspace would have no remaining owners and must throw.

Suspending a non-owner returns early without emitting an activity. Reinstating an already active member is idempotent and returns unchanged. Reinstating an invited member should not be treated as active; only members with status "active" will no-op.

Reinstating an invited member will return unchanged rather than activating them, since the specification does not define that transition. Archived members must be rejected with a NotFound error, as findMemberById returns archived records. The specific error type for self-suspension and outranking refusals still needs to be determined.

countActiveMembers currently only counts members with an active status.

Seat counts must include suspended members. I will update countActiveMembers or add a new function and switch call sites. Tests should remain unaffected since fixtures only contain active members.

Usage recompute and organization summary memberCount will also be updated to count suspended members. Invited members remain excluded. Removed members retain suspended status while archived, so they still occupy seats.

notify() must skip suspended recipients for any notification kind on any channel.

Digest also skips suspended recipients. The notification service needs the member repository to look up membership status. Digest filtering should happen in listDigestRecipients and buildDigest, and direct buildDigest calls must skip suspended users too.

Digest emails are sent from existing unread notifications without creating new rows. buildDigest returns null for suspended recipients, so their unread messages remain untouched and will be digested once reinstated. The org switcher should also exclude suspended users from listOrgsForUser.

Determining the correct error type for self-refusal and outrank cases.

Settled on a plain Error with a stable message for self-refusal and outrank cases, matching the last-owner pattern. Tests will match against `/cannot suspend/`. Need a `setStatus` helper to return members idempotently without emitting when suspending or reinstating.

Updating member queries to include suspended status. `countActiveMembers` will count active and suspended members. `listOrgsForUser` excludes suspended members. `notify` skips suspended recipients before preference checks. Digest checks member status. Removed members may still have preferences.

Issue service checks member status before writes. `createIssue` validates assignee before insertion. `assignIssue` validates assignee before assignment. Unassigning null is allowed. Reassigning the same suspended user may still trigger a write.

Assigning an existing issue to a suspended member throws MemberSuspendedError before any write occurs. Reassigning the same suspended user is blocked even if already assigned. Assigning to an active member still writes and emits as before. The suspension refusal order is: scope, not found or removed, permission, self, outrank, idempotent, last owner, then write and emit.

The idempotent check for already-suspended members must precede the last-owner check. If an admin outranks a suspended owner, the refusal still returns the member unchanged without emitting.

An already-suspended member outranked by an admin still returns unchanged. The spec treats this as a no-op, so permission and self-refusal checks run before the idempotent return.

The idempotent check for already-suspended members will run after the authority guards so unauthorized callers still receive errors while authorized callers get the no-op return. For removed members, the spec throws NotFoundError before checking permission, and `findMemberById` returns archived members so the removed check must come after the permission check.

The removed-member check will run immediately after the lookup so both missing and removed members throw NotFound before any permission check. Self-refusal compares user IDs directly. Outrank checks use ROLE_RANK to compare member and actor roles.

Adding MemberSuspendedError mapping so actions can catch it and resolve code conflicts.

The MemberSuspendedError class belongs in member-service.ts. No circular import issues arise from this placement. Webhook fanout should target events, not notifications. The assignee picker will list all members from the server-side member list, including suspended ones, since the UI restriction is only a manifest comment.

Activity labels need new keys added to compile. The member.joined listener is missing from the snippet and will not be fixed. setMemberStatus will throw a plain Error for self-refusals to prevent publishing.

Suspend requires calling hasRoleAtLeast. The permission check uses hasRoleAtLeast(actor.role, member.role). This blocks refusal when the member outranks the actor and allows it otherwise.

The suspend path will reuse the existing hasRoleAtLeast call from updateMemberRole. Platform staff follow the same permission rules. Suspended members are excluded from mention resolution by filtering the member list before resolveMentions. Digest-service needs a memberRepo import, and the notification-service notify loop requires updates.

organization-repository needs a status filter. issue-service will import MemberSuspendedError and memberRepo, skip null assigneeId in createIssue, and throw the error from its assignment path.

Implementing all edits now. Checking membership status.

Adding the missing activity listener and exhaustive switch tests. Activity labels and Zod enums need new action keys. Event maps require updated event definitions. Member status updates will follow the same pattern as role changes. Reinstating a member clears its archived state. Archived members are filtered from findMemberById.

The last owner remaining check excludes suspended owners only. Invited owners still count as active workspace owners.
